Bill status, H.R. 9171, Department of the Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2027

status_summary: No bill authorizing humane disposal of excess wild horses and burros was found. The fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 budget requests omitted the long-standing appropriations language barring sale for slaughter, per news reports of 2025-06-03 and 2026-09-02, but Congress kept the restriction in the final fiscal 2026 law, Public Law 119-74 (enacted 2026-01-23), according to the 2026-09-02 report. The House Appropriations Committee reported H.R. 9171, the fiscal 2027 Interior bill, on 2026-06-05, and it was placed on the Union Calendar with no later floor action; the 2026-09-02 report says it retains a bar on destroying excess animals for commercial products. BLM estimates 85,466 animals on its lands as of 2026-03-01 and 58,025 held off the range as of May 2026, and reports 7,853 removals and 8,080 placements into private care in fiscal 2025.

timeline.event: Reporting said the fiscal 2026 BLM budget request omitted the appropriations language barring sale or transfer of wild horses and burros for slaughter.
BLM estimated 85,466 wild horses and burros on its managed lands (fiscal 2026 estimate).

The House Appropriations Committee reported H.R. 9171, the fiscal 2027 Interior appropriations bill (H. Rept. 119-687), and it was placed on the Union Calendar (Calendar No. 599); no disposal authority was found in the portions of the text read.

Reporting said the fiscal 2027 budget request again omitted the slaughter restriction, that Congress kept it in the final fiscal 2026 law, and that the House Appropriations Committee's fiscal 2027 Interior bill retains the bar on destroying excess animals for commercial products.

title: Seek law allowing humane disposal of excess wild horses and burros
uncertainties: The budget-request omissions and the retention of the slaughter restriction in Public Law 119-74 and H.R. 9171 are reported by two news outlets; the wild horse and burro provisos in the statute and the reported bill could not be located because the govinfo.gov text of Public Law 119-74 returned only part of Division A, and the budget justification documents were not opened. The enactment date of Public Law 119-74 and the reporting of H.R. 9171 on 2026-06-05 were confirmed on govinfo.gov.
